items.summary:
It was discovered that Yodl incorrectly handled certain input, leading to a
buffer over-read. An attacker could possibly use this issue to cause Yodl
to crash, resulting in a denial of service.

items.title: USN-9062-1: SNMPTT vulnerability
items.summary:
It was discovered that SNMPTT did not properly sanitize trap data passed to
commands run through the EXEC, PREEXEC, and unknown_trap_exec options. A
remote attacker could possibly use this issue to execute arbitrary shell
commands.

items.title: USN-9060-1: kramdown vulnerability
items.summary:
It was discovered that kramdown processed the template option in documents
by default. An attacker could possibly use this issue to read arbitrary
files or execute arbitrary code.

items.title: USN-9059-1: ruby-jwt vulnerability
items.summary:
It was discovered that ruby-jwt incorrectly verified HMAC signatures when
the verification key was empty or missing. A remote attacker could possibly
use this issue to forge tokens and bypass authentication.

items.title: USN-9058-1: Action Pack Page Caching vulnerability
items.summary:
It was discovered that Action Pack Page Caching incorrectly handled certain
request paths when writing cached pages. A remote attacker could possibly
use this issue to write arbitrary files to the web server, and possibly
execute arbitrary code.

items.title: USN-9057-1: rkhunter vulnerability
items.summary:
It was discovered that rkhunter downloaded mirror updates over an insecure
channel. A remote attacker could possibly use this issue to execute
arbitrary code.

items.title: USN-9055-1: pecl_http vulnerability
items.summary:
It was discovered that pecl_http incorrectly handled certain HTTP request
parameters, leading to a type confusion. A remote attacker could possibly
use this issue to cause PHP to crash, resulting in a denial of service, or
execute arbitrary code.

items.title: USN-9054-1: Babel vulnerability
items.summary:
It was discovered that Babel incorrectly evaluated certain code during
compilation when used with certain plugins. If a user or an automated
system were tricked into compiling specially crafted code, an attacker
could possibly use this issue to execute arbitrary code.

items.title: USN-9053-1: NetworkManager-ssh vulnerability
items.summary:
It was discovered that NetworkManager-ssh did not properly validate extra
options in VPN connection settings. A local attacker could possibly use
this issue to escalate privileges.

items.summary: Led by the German Itzehoe Public Prosecutor's Office (Staatsanwaltschaft Itzehoe), the operation targeted a company suspected of supplying fraudulent trading websites to criminal groups. items.title: Not a game: Europol and partners target terrorist role-playing online
items.summary: Europol’s European Union Internet Referral Unit (EU IRU) coordinated together with Spain a Referral Action Day targeting violent extremist and terrorist live action role-playing (LARPing) in online gaming environments. Specialised units from 16 countries participated in the action.

items.title: Five TEFAF robbery suspects added to EU Most Wanted
items.summary: As of 29 October 2026, five new fugitives, four men and one woman, have been added to the EU Most Wanted list. According to the Limburg Public Prosecutor's Office (Openbaar Ministerie) and the Dutch Police (Politie), all five suspects are involved in the European Fine Art Fair (TEFAF) robbery that took place on 28 June 2022 in Maastricht, the Netherlands.

items.title: 27 arrests and 248 potential victims identified in action week against labour exploitation
items.summary: Europol, the European Labour Authority (ELA), and 34 participating countries today announced the results of an action week targeting human trafficking for labour exploitation. The operation, part of an EMPACT action led by Sweden, brought together police, border guards, labour and social security inspectorates, and tax authorities to crack down on exploitative practices in high-risk sectors such as agriculture, construction, cosmetic services, massage parlours, and hospitality.

items.title: 5th EMPACT Hackathon leads to the detection of 51 potential victims
items.summary: An international operation involving 40 experts and investigators from 20 countries has identified 51 potential victims of human trafficking, as well as five suspects. Held in Amsterdam from 23 to 25 September 2026, the fifth EMPACT Hackathon against the digital aspects of human trafficking brought together police officers, labour authorities and specialists in online investigations, supported by Europol and Eurojust.

items.title: Almost 50 arrested as police target Western Balkan network linked to killings
items.summary: Nearly 50 suspects have been arrested in an international operation targeting a drug trafficking network with Western Balkan members, linked to killings, kidnappings and grenade attacks across Europe.

items.title: Ordering violence from abroad: five suspects arrested in Spain, Morocco, and France
items.summary:
Five suspects linked to the organisation and recruitment of serious violence have been arrested in Spain, Morocco, and France, in the latest results of the Operational Taskforce (OTF) GRIMM, coordinated by Europol.

The arrests in August and September target the upper levels of violence-as-a-service: those suspected of ordering attacks, finding perpetrators and coordinating crimes from abroad. Among those apprehended are fugitives featured on the EU Most Wanted website.
